columns.text: Marie Matusz works with display and context as her material, and describes her practice as "placing things at a distance that we can get closer to." The site is built from that sentence: a single continuous space in which her works hang at depth in a dark field, and scrolling is the act of approach. Reaching a work and opening it is one unbroken gesture. The clicked image carries itself into its gallery, its companion images are born from the same vanishing point everything else comes from, and on closing nothing retreats: every image expands past the viewer and exits the frame.

Underneath, the apparatus is conventional web technology held to unusual discipline: a scroll-driven depth index with a critically damped camera, shared-element transitions in place of page navigation, and an idle preloader that decodes the entire catalog before it is asked for, so no approach is ever interrupted by loading. The interface withholds itself; the work stays the brightest thing on screen.
